recent_posts.title: How to use Kagai to test vibe coded apps
recent_posts.summary: Vibe-coded apps built with AI tools are fast to create but prone to security issues, broken flows, and poor test coverage. Kagai (testmu.ai) is a GenAI-native testing tool that lets you describe tests in natural language, auto-generates test cases, executes them, and flags bugs. Key features include AI test case generation from text prompts or documents, multi-step scenario execution, auto-healing tests that adapt to UI changes, automatic bug detection, and API testing. A walkthrough demonstrates testing a simple task manager app, covering tab isolation, UI state verification, and Supabase API validation. A 7-day free trial is available.

recent_posts.title: Yesim eSIM review for digital nomads and frequent travelers
recent_posts.summary: A digital nomad shares her experience using Yesim, a Swiss-based eSIM service, after a year of remote work travel. She explains how eSIMs work, walks through Yesim's plan options (single country, regional, global, global plus, and pay-as-you-go), and shares performance observations including 5G speeds, automatic carrier switching, and real-time data tracking. She also notes limitations: coverage depends on local infrastructure and the phone must support eSIM. A referral discount code is offered.

recent_posts.title: Neo browser review: an AI-native alternative to Google Chrome
recent_posts.summary: A sponsored walkthrough of Neo, an AI-native browser created by Norton, presented as a replacement for Google Chrome. Key features include cross-tab intelligence for navigating and summarizing multiple tabs simultaneously, a magic box for AI-powered search and Q&A, local AI processing for privacy, a personalized news feed, and Norton Web Shield for security. The browser is free on Mac and Windows and syncs with existing Chrome data via Google account login.

recent_posts.title: 5 practical shortcuts for learning AWS faster and cheaper
recent_posts.summary: Five practical tips for learning AWS more efficiently: (1) Maximize the AWS free tier by using always-free services like Lambda and DynamoDB, and cycling new accounts for credits. (2) Automate diagram-to-documentation workflows using tools like Miro Flows. (3) Match your learning style to the method — hands-on chaos engineering with AWS Fault Injection Simulator, gamified learning with AWS Cloud Quest, or audio learning via NotebookLM. (4) Use AI tools like Claude or ChatGPT as a personal tutor, code generator, and debugger to accelerate cloud work. (5) Tap into the AWS community through Discord, Slack, and the AWS Community Builders program to avoid learning in isolation.

recent_posts.title: Build an automated AWS news dashboard with Warp and Oz agents
recent_posts.summary: A walkthrough of building an automated AWS cloud news dashboard using Warp terminal and its Oz agent orchestration platform. The tutorial covers setting up Oz, using AI agents to generate the dashboard code, running parallel cloud agents for additional tasks (news ticker, security scan), deploying via GitHub Pages with GitHub Actions, and scheduling a daily agent to auto-update the news feed. A real-time agent session sharing/collaboration feature is also demonstrated.

recent_posts.title: 90-day roadmap to become a cloud solutions architect
recent_posts.summary: A 90-day roadmap for becoming a cloud solutions architect, covering three phases: building AWS fundamentals and learning infrastructure-as-code with Terraform in month one, building and documenting real-world cloud projects in month two, and job preparation including resume writing, interview practice, and networking in month three. The guide emphasizes that the 2026 hiring bar demands both technical skills and soft skills like relationship-building, plus familiarity with AI tools such as AWS Bedrock and SageMaker to stand out from other candidates.

recent_posts.title: How to build your own Custom AI Assistant (Fine-Tune LLM Tutorial)
recent_posts.summary: A walkthrough tutorial on fine-tuning a custom LLM using the FPT AI Factory platform. Using a Jupyter notebook environment with an H200 GPU, the process covers preparing Q&A training data, formatting it as JSONL, and fine-tuning the Mistral model with LoRA adapters to create a domain-specific interview coaching assistant. The tutorial demonstrates that LoRA allows efficient fine-tuning by adding a small expert layer rather than retraining the full model, keeping costs and time low. FPT AI Factory is the sponsored platform providing $100 in free credits for users to follow along.

recent_posts.title: 10 app ideas you can build with vibe coding in under 10 minutes
recent_posts.summary: A beginner-friendly walkthrough of 10 app ideas you can build using vibe coding with no programming knowledge, all using the Mocha AI app builder platform. App ideas include an AI travel itinerary planner, 30-day challenge site, expense tracker, resume roaster, Linktree clone, FIRE retirement calculator, blog-to-podcast converter, focus music player, tech news dashboard, and a paid newsletter site. The video also demonstrates Mocha's features including built-in database, email functionality, analytics, and one-click deployment.

recent_posts.title: How to create and sell AI coloring books on Amazon KDP using Book Bolt
recent_posts.summary: A walkthrough on building an AI-powered coloring book side business using Amazon KDP and Book Bolt. Covers niche research using keyword and competition data, generating coloring book pages with AI image tools, and publishing the finished product on Amazon KDP with no upfront inventory costs. Also touches on other book types like Sudoku, journals, and puzzle books that can be created with the same platform.

recent_posts.title: Why the AWS Solutions Architect Professional certification won't get you hired
recent_posts.summary: A former Amazon solutions architect argues that the AWS Solutions Architect Professional certification is largely useless for career advancement. Despite its prestige, the exam can be gamed through pattern recognition and AI tools, and employers increasingly view certifications without hands-on experience as a red flag. Instead, the recommended approach is a 20/40/40 split: 20% theory, 40% hands-on projects, and 40% networking, personal branding, and interview prep. The AWS Cloud Practitioner and Solutions Architect Associate certifications are sufficient as a foundation before moving directly to real-world projects.
